enonce_intro_markdown:
Given that figure 1 represents the height PR of a boy 1.8 m and his shadow RQ, 2.4 m long, on a flat horizontal ground.

![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_4_fig_1.png)

figures.legende: Figure 1: right-angled triangle PRQ with the right angle at R; PR = 1.8 m (the boy), RQ = 2.4 m (his shadow), PQ joins the tip of the head to the end of the shadow.

questions.corrige_markdown:
The boy stands vertically on flat ground, so triangle PRQ has a right angle at R. By Pythagoras' theorem:

$PQ^2=PR^2+RQ^2=1.8^2+2.4^2=3.24+5.76=9$

$PQ=\sqrt{9}=3$ m.

**Answer: $PQ=3$ m.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Calculate the angle of elevation of the sun from Q to the tip of the boy's head P, leaving your answer to the nearest degree *[5 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The angle of elevation is the angle $\theta=\angle PQR$ at Q between the ground $QR$ and the line of sight $QP$.

$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\dfrac{PR}{RQ}=\dfrac{1.8}{2.4}=0.75$

$\theta=\tan^{-1}(0.75)=36.87^\circ\approx 37^\circ$ (nearest degree).

**Answer: $37^\circ$.**
